app.title: Lincoln World Model
app.description: Unofficial student-made 3D map of the buildings of Lincoln University's Lincoln campus, drawn from OpenStreetMap. Not affiliated with Lincoln University.
app.ogDescription: See the buildings of Lincoln University's Lincoln campus on a 3D model of the place, drawn from OpenStreetMap. Unofficial; not affiliated with Lincoln University.
app.noscript: Lincoln World Model is an unofficial 3D map of the buildings of Lincoln University's Lincoln campus. It needs JavaScript and WebGL to run. It is not affiliated with Lincoln University.
app.loadError: The map data could not be loaded. Check your connection and reload the page.
app.noWebgl: This browser could not start WebGL, so the 3D map is not shown. Search for buildings still works.
app.sceneLabel: 3D map of Lincoln University's Lincoln campus. Drag to rotate, scroll or pinch to zoom, right-drag or two fingers to move.

about.unofficial: Lincoln World Model is made by a student for students. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or maintained by Lincoln University, and it uses no Lincoln logo. Its colours are the project's own, the same for every school, and none is taken from Lincoln. It shows the University's Lincoln campus from OpenStreetMap, and shows a building as the University's only where OpenStreetMap tags it as the University's; the other buildings on the campus are drawn as surroundings, with no name. For anything that matters, check Lincoln's own campus maps and your own timetable.

limits.timetable: No class times. Lincoln's online timetable is open to read, but it gives a class's day, time and room only after its form is sent, and its terms are on Lincoln's main website, which its robots.txt closes to this project. So the terms are unread, and the site does not take the timetable. Nothing here is made up to fill the gap.
limits.timetableLoaded: Class times come from a snapshot of Lincoln's timetable taken on {date}. Rooms and times change during the semester; your own timetable is the authority.
limits.scheduled: A timetabled class is not the same as an occupied room. Classes are cancelled, moved and held online, and rooms are used for things that are not on the timetable.
limits.heights: Each of Lincoln's buildings is one block on its OpenStreetMap outline, with no floors. Its height comes from OpenStreetMap: its height tag where it has one; else its number of levels, {height} m each; else 6.5 m, or 10 m for a building over 900 m², the defaults of the surrounding buildings. The building card says which. None of these heights is surveyed: OpenStreetMap gives three of Lincoln's buildings a number of levels and none a height, so the other five stand at a default. The windows and the rim round each roof are drawn by rule and say nothing about the real walls and roofs. The ground's heights come from Land Information New Zealand's 8 m elevation model of 2012, which is drawn from contours: it is smooth bare ground, with sharp peaks a few metres low. A building stands on the ground under its middle; on a slope its uphill side goes into the hill and a footing fills the gap below the other side.
limits.rooms: No floors and no rooms. Lincoln's campus maps are on its main website, which its robots.txt closes to this project, and its online timetable shows its rooms only after its form is sent. So each building is one block, and nothing inside it is drawn.
limits.campuses: The Lincoln campus is modelled. Its buildings and their outlines come from OpenStreetMap, and a building is drawn as Lincoln University's only where OpenStreetMap tags it as the University's: where it names Lincoln University as its operator, or tags it as a university building (building=university), and gives it a name. That makes 8 of the campus's 163 buildings. Every other building on the campus is drawn among the surrounding buildings, with no name: among them many large buildings in its middle, which OpenStreetMap does not tag as the University's or leaves unnamed. So are Memorial Hall, which OpenStreetMap maps as disused, and the building OpenStreetMap names AgResearch, the name of another body. Halls of residence and childcare centres stay unnamed among the surroundings. The University's own campus map is on its main website, which its robots.txt closes to this project, so the site does not use it. The University's places away from the campus are not modelled.
limits.context: Surrounding buildings, streets and trees come from OpenStreetMap. Where it maps a building in parts or gives a roof a shape, those are drawn, the roof in a simplified form. Where a height is not mapped, a default is used. In the walker views every building, Lincoln's and the rest, is drawn with storeys from its height, windows, and walls of plaster, brick, concrete, stone, glass or weatherboard chosen by rule from where it stands; none of it says what a real building looks like, and there are no doors, since none are mapped. The ground there is drawn by rule as well, on the streets, paths, railways, parks and ponds OpenStreetMap maps: asphalt with white lines, kerbs, paving slabs, steps, sleepers and rails, lawns and water, and grass and bare earth elsewhere. Its widths, lines and kerbs say nothing about the real ones, and there are no crossings, arrows or signs, since none are mapped. A tree standing alone is where OpenStreetMap maps it; its size and shape are drawn by rule, and in the walker views so are its leaves, its bark and the way it sways in a light breeze, the same every day; none of it says what kind of tree it is. Trees OpenStreetMap tags as deciduous turn in April and May, stand bare from June to August and come into leaf in September and October; the rest are drawn evergreen. Trees inside woodland areas are scattered for decoration.
limits.walker: The walker is a made-up figure, not a person: it stands for nobody, and nothing about where it goes leaves your browser. Its walks are planned round the buildings on the map and along OpenStreetMap's paths and streets, off motorways except over footbridges. Doors and entrances are not mapped, so a walk to a building ends beside its nearest wall, and it passes gates, fences and kerbs the map does not have. Its body is the "Animated Human" model by Quaternius, given to the public domain (CC0); its stance, trainers, hair, mouth, backpack and umbrella are drawn here by rule, in the project's own colours, none taken from Lincoln. Where a building or a tree hides it, its shape shows through. It can also ride a made-up electric scooter on the same ways, at up to 25 km/h, or fly a made-up drone in its place, up to 120 m above the ground and over the roofs as high as the map draws them, which for most buildings are estimated. Neither is any real make, and their colours are the project's own. An agent can steer it on your own computer through the scripts in the source code.
limits.subjects: No course list. Lincoln's course pages are on its main website, which its robots.txt closes to this project. Its online timetable lists course codes without their titles, and its terms are unread, so the site does not take them.
limits.calendar: No semester dates. Lincoln's key dates are on its main website, which its robots.txt closes to this project, so the site does not take them, and the time panel moves the sun and the light only.
limits.daylight: The sun stands where it does over Lincoln University's Lincoln campus at the date and time shown, from NOAA's published solar-position equations; below 10° above the horizon it is drawn at 10°, so that shadows stay on the map. Night falls as the sun goes from 6° above the horizon to 8° below. In Now mode the cloud, rain and fog follow Open-Meteo's current weather for the Lincoln campus, and the falling rain is drawn by rule; Preview shows a clear sky, because past and future weather are not known here.

about.privacy: The site has no accounts and sets no cookies. It holds no names of people. Only the copy at campusworldmodel.com is counted: there Cloudflare, which serves the site, counts page views and visits with its Web Analytics. It stores nothing in your browser and does not record which building you look at; a content blocker may stop it. If the weather line is shown, your browser asks Open-Meteo for the current weather at Lincoln University's Lincoln campus; nothing about you is sent beyond that request. A walk with the walker stays in your browser: where it goes, what it says and what it wears are not sent anywhere.

room.noTimetableWhy: Lincoln's class times are not taken by this site, so it cannot say what is scheduled here. See About for details.

search.hint: Type a building's name, for example Ivey Hall or Forbes Building. Rooms and courses are not shown: see About.
search.noResultsHint: Lincoln University's buildings are found by the names OpenStreetMap gives them, and only the ones it tags as the University's are on the map. Building names work with or without macrons.
